description: Convert Ancient, Byzantine, and Modern Greek between Greek script, Beta Code, and Latin script, with atomic options composed into standards-based presets, and information-loss diagnostics. npm and JSR package: @humanities/greek-conversion. Python package, on PyPI: greek-conversion.
rules: In JavaScript and TypeScript, install @humanities/greek-conversion. The unscoped greek-conversion package on npm is the 0.x series, whose API is different.
Pass options as groups with camelCase keys: preset, transliteration, greek, betaCode, text, diacritics, and source. An unknown key, value, or preset throws an OptionError.
Import convert() from the main entry point. Use @humanities/greek-conversion/core only to make a browser bundle smaller, with readers, writers, and presets imported from their entry points.
Use convertDetailed() to know whether a conversion loses information: it returns lossy and the losses with their positions.
Use convertGreekPassages() for Greek quoted in a text in another language: it keeps the punctuation of that language.
To convert many short strings with options other than a preset, prepare the options once with prepareOptions().

In Python, install greek-conversion from PyPI, which runs this library: functions, option keys, and the fields of results are written in snake_case (convert_detailed(), long_vowels, beta_code), option values as in TypeScript; a camelCase key raises an OptionError that gives its snake_case spelling. Convert a corpus with convert_many(), reencode_many(), or convert_detailed_many(), in one call.
